title: Specified geometric 2-isomorphism comparison on derived modules
statement: For normalized lifts of h,k : X → Y and a specified isomorphism theta : h.inverse ≅ k.inverse with h.ringMap = theta followed by k.ringMap, there is an ordinary scalar-extension isomorphism normalized by theta on insertions. Its localization gives a derived pullback isomorphism with the flat-term K-flat representative formula, compatible with tensor and unit. The ordinary and derived right comparisons are its adjunction mates; the latter has the right-derived unit formula on every complex. No unspecified equivalence replaces theta. The recorded presentations, edges, representative models and normalization equations are those defined in [def-sfb-ringed-derived-comparison-data].

source.place: Modules on Sites, Tags 03D7, 03D8 and 03EL; Cohomology on Sites, Tags 07A4 and 07A6; original comparison proof steps 12–13

proof.text: Construct the identity geometric ringed-topos morphism i on X explicitly. Its ring map, set inverse image and module direct image are identities. Obtain a normalized lift li using the adjoint-lift and tensor-lift existence declarations and the site's recorded tensor model. Apply identity normalization to li. Apply composition normalization to li, lk, lh with geometric path theta followed by the inverse identity unitor and the inverse identity comparison. Naturality of the identity comparison and the given structural-map equality verify the composition ring-map hypothesis.

Compose the ordinary and derived composition isomorphisms with the identity-normalization isomorphisms, whiskered on the left by k's pullback, and the right unitor. The composition insertion equation followed by the identity insertion equation simplifies by naturality to exactly the specified theta insertion equation. Pullback preserves the flat-term K-flat class. At such a complex use the identity comparison on k's pulled-back complex, then the composition representative formula; termwise equality of the ordinary maps identifies their localized composite with the required ordinary comparison. The explicit-site versus monoidal tensor comparison transports termwise flatness between the two conventions.

Use adjunction conjugation for the ordinary right comparison. Conjugation respects composition, whiskering and the identity unitor, so the inverse derived right mate factors as the composition right mate followed by k's right functor applied to the identity right mate. Apply the composition eta equation and the identity eta equation at the given complex. Naturality of k's eta moves the identity chain map through the derived right functor. The same conjugation factorization degreewise identifies the resulting ordinary chain map with the inverse ordinary right comparison. Cancel the invertible mates to obtain the required pushforward formula on every complex.

For tensor compatibility move the identity comparison through k's tensorator by naturality, substitute the identity tensor equation, and apply the composition tensor equation. Functoriality of the tensor combines the two pairs of comparison components. For the unit move the identity comparison through k's unit map, then substitute the identity and composition unit equations. Assemble these maps and equations into TwoIsoCore.
